# /techlead-loop Command

Autonomous feature delivery loop for the Tech Lead agent. Orchestrates all agents (frontend, backend, tester, reviewer) through their complete lifecycle.

## Usage

```bash
/techlead-loop "Feature description" [--max-iterations <n>] [--completion-promise "<text>"]
```

## Parameters

- `<feature-description>` - Description of the feature to implement (required)
- `--max-iterations <n>` - Maximum iterations before timeout (recommended: 50, prevents infinite loops)
- `--completion-promise "<text>"` - Signal text to exit loop (default: "FEATURE_COMPLETE")

## Example

```bash
/techlead-loop "Add email notifications when users make suggestions" --max-iterations 50 --completion-promise "FEATURE_COMPLETE"
```

## How It Works

The Tech Lead agent runs in a self-referential loop:

1. **Iteration 1 (Analysis & Planning)**
   - Tech Lead analyzes the feature request
   - Creates epic + implementation beads
   - Presents plan to user
   - Waits for user to say "approved"
   - Since "approved" not found, loop continues

2. **Iteration 2+ (Orchestration)**
   - Tech Lead checks if user approved (looks for "approved" in conversation)
   - If approved: Invokes @frontend and @backend in parallel
   - Polls bead status every 30 seconds via `bd show`
   - When both report `ready`: Invokes @tester
   - Monitors tester progress
   - When tester reports `ready`: Invokes @reviewer
   - Monitors reviewer progress
   - If reviewer closes beads: Asks user "Ready to commit?"
   - If issues found: Identifies responsible agent, reassigns, re-invokes reviewer
   - Loop continues until completion promise is output

3. **Final Iteration (Completion)**
   - Tech Lead outputs: `<promise>FEATURE_COMPLETE</promise>`
   - Stop hook detects this exact string
   - Loop exits
   - User can now see all completed work

## Stop Hook

The system includes a stop hook that:
- Checks for `<promise>FEATURE_COMPLETE</promise>` in output
- If found: Allows normal exit (work is complete)
- If not found: Re-feeds the entire prompt to Tech Lead
- Enforces `--max-iterations` limit for safety

## Agent Invocation Sequence

```
Iteration 1: Planning
  ├─ Analyze feature
  ├─ Create beads
  ├─ Present plan
  └─ Wait for approval

Iteration 2+: Orchestration (after "approved")
  ├─ Invoke @frontend and @backend (parallel)
  ├─ Poll both until ready (max 120 min)
  ├─ Invoke @tester
  ├─ Poll tester until ready (max 120 min)
  ├─ Invoke @reviewer
  ├─ Poll reviewer until beads closed (max 30 min)
  │  ├─ If issues found:
  │  │  ├─ Identify responsible agent
  │  │  ├─ Reassign bead
  │  │  ├─ Re-invoke @reviewer
  │  │  └─ Loop until all pass
  │  └─ If all pass: Ask user to commit
  ├─ After user says "commit": Commit changes
  └─ Output completion promise

Loop: Exits when <promise>FEATURE_COMPLETE</promise> found or max-iterations reached
```

## Status Polling

Tech Lead polls bead status using:

```bash
bd show {bead-id}  # Check status field for: open, in_progress, ready, closed
```

Polling strategy:
- Check status every 30 seconds
- Timeout per phase: 120 minutes (frontend/backend), 120 minutes (tester), 30 minutes (reviewer)
- If timeout occurs, notify user of stalled agent

## Issue Resolution Loop

If reviewer finds issues:

```
Reviewer: bd comment {bead-id} --body "Issues found: ..."
  ↓
Tech Lead: Reads comments
  ↓
Tech Lead: Identifies responsible agent:
  - UI/components/pages → @frontend
  - Server actions/schemas/database → @backend
  - Tests/coverage → @tester
  ↓
Tech Lead: bd assign {bead-id} @{agent-name}
  ↓
Tech Lead: @{agent-name} - Issues found. See {bead-id} comments.
  ↓
Agent: Fixes issues → bd status ready
  ↓
Tech Lead: @reviewer review {bead-id}
  ↓
Reviewer: Validates → closes or reports new issues
  ↓
Loop: Repeat until all pass
```

## Success Criteria

Loop exits successfully when Tech Lead outputs:

```
<promise>FEATURE_COMPLETE</promise>
```

This indicates:
- ✓ All beads created
- ✓ User approved plan
- ✓ Frontend implemented and reported ready
- ✓ Backend implemented and reported ready
- ✓ Tester wrote tests and reported ready
- ✓ Reviewer ran all quality gates and closed beads
- ✓ User approved commit
- ✓ Changes committed to git

## Failure Scenarios

Loop exits with failure if:

1. **Max iterations reached** - Feature took too long, likely stalled agent
   - Check which agent was last working
   - Manually invoke that agent to resume

2. **Agent timeout** - Agent didn't report ready within time limit
   - Check `bd show {bead-id}` to see current status
   - Manually invoke agent if needed

3. **User interruption** - User says "cancel" or "stop"
   - Tech Lead should exit gracefully
   - All beads remain in their current state
   - Can resume later by manually invoking agents

## Example Session

```
User: /techlead-loop "Add email notifications" --max-iterations 50

Tech Lead (Iteration 1):
  Analyzing feature request...
  Creating beads...

  ## Plan: Email Notifications Feature

  ### Beads Created
  - vamsa-epic-123: Email notifications for suggestions
  - vamsa-frontend-124: UI for notification preferences
  - vamsa-backend-125: Email service + database model

  ### Acceptance Criteria
  - [ ] User receives email when suggestion created
  - [ ] User can disable notifications in settings
  - [ ] Professional email template with unsubscribe link

  Reply "approved" to proceed, or provide feedback.

User: approved

Tech Lead (Iteration 2+):
  Plan approved! Invoking agents...

  @frontend implement vamsa-frontend-124
  @backend implement vamsa-backend-125

  Waiting for implementations... checking status every 30 seconds.

Tech Lead (Iteration 3+):
  Frontend status: in_progress
  Backend status: in_progress

Tech Lead (Iteration 4+):
  Frontend status: ready ✓
  Backend status: ready ✓

  Both implementations complete! Invoking tester...

  @tester write tests for vamsa-epic-123

  Waiting for tests... checking status every 30 seconds.

Tech Lead (Iteration 5+):
  Tester status: ready ✓
  Coverage: Statements 94%, Branches 88%, Functions 96%, Lines 94%

  Tests complete! Invoking reviewer...

  @reviewer review vamsa-epic-123

  Waiting for review... checking status every 30 seconds.

Tech Lead (Iteration 6+):
  Reviewer status: closed ✓
  All quality gates passed!

  Ready to commit?

User: commit

Tech Lead (Iteration 7+):
  Committing changes...
  git add .
  git commit -m "feat: add email notifications..."
  bd sync
  git push

  <promise>FEATURE_COMPLETE</promise>

Loop exits. Feature complete!
```

## Comparison: Manual vs Loop

### Manual Approach (Current)
```
User → Tech Lead: "Add feature"
Tech Lead: Creates beads, presents plan
User: "approved"
User: "@frontend implement vamsa-123"
User: (waits, monitors bd show vamsa-123)
User: "@backend implement vamsa-124"
User: (waits, monitors bd show vamsa-124)
User: (when both ready) "@tester write tests"
User: (waits, monitors bd show vamsa-epic)
User: (when ready) "@reviewer review vamsa-epic"
User: (waits, monitors for closure)
User: Tech Lead commits
```

**Time:** User must manually coordinate all handoffs
**Effort:** High - requires constant monitoring

### Loop Approach (New)
```
User: /techlead-loop "Add feature"
Tech Lead: Creates beads, presents plan
User: "approved"
Tech Lead: Orchestrates ALL agents automatically
Tech Lead: Monitors status, handles issues, coordinates fixes
Tech Lead: Commits changes when ready
Tech Lead: Outputs completion promise
Loop: Exits
```

**Time:** Fully autonomous orchestration
**Effort:** Zero - user just approves plan and waits

## Tech Lead System Prompt Updates

The Tech Lead agent's system prompt is enhanced with:

1. **Loop Detection** - Understand when running in loop mode
2. **Status Polling** - Instructions on checking `bd show` every 30 seconds
3. **Automatic Invocation** - When to invoke each agent
4. **Issue Management** - How to identify and reassign issues
5. **Completion Signal** - When to output the completion promise

See: `.opencode/agent/techlead.md` for full updated prompt.

## Requirements

- `bd` (beads CLI) - Must be installed and configured
- All agent configs in `.opencode/agent/` - Must be present
- Stop hook - Must be configured to detect completion promise
- Permissions - Tech Lead must have permission for `bd *` and `bun run *` commands

## Troubleshooting

### Loop seems stuck (iterations keep increasing)

Check:
1. Did user say "approved"? Tech Lead is waiting for this.
2. Check bead status: `bd show {bead-id}` - Is agent actually working?
3. Check agent logs to see what they're doing
4. If agent is stuck, manually invoke them again
5. Loop will continue polling until agent reports ready

### Agent didn't start

Check:
1. Did Tech Lead actually invoke the agent? Look for `@agent-name` mention
2. Check if agent config exists in `.opencode/agent/`
3. Check permissions - agent may not have access to required commands

### Agent is working but loop keeps polling

This is normal! Loop continues until agent reports status `ready`.
- Agent typically reports within 1-2 hours for implementation
- Loop keeps polling, Tech Lead is patient

### Want to manually intervene

You can:
1. Manually invoke any agent: `@agent-name do-something`
2. Manually update bead status: `bd status {id} ready`
3. Tech Lead will see the change on next poll and continue

### Want to exit loop early

Say: "cancel" - Tech Lead will exit gracefully without completing the loop.

---

## See Also

- `ARCHITECTURE.md` - System design and concepts
- `WORKFLOW.md` - Manual workflow reference
- `GOVERNANCE.md` - Why only reviewer closes beads
- `.opencode/agent/techlead.md` - Tech Lead system prompt with orchestration logic

## GEDCOM Import/Export Implementation Plan

### Feature Overview

GEDCOM (Genealogical Data Communication) is the de facto standard for exchanging genealogical data between different software applications. This feature will enable vamsa users to:

1. **Import GEDCOM files** (.ged) from other genealogy software (Ancestry, FamilySearch, Gramps, etc.)
2. **Export vamsa data** to GEDCOM 5.5.1 format for use in other applications

### GEDCOM Format Summary

GEDCOM uses a hierarchical text format with the following key structures:

```
0 HEAD
1 SOUR vamsa
1 GEDC
2 VERS 5.5.1
2 FORM LINEAGE-LINKED
1 CHAR UTF-8

0 @I1@ INDI
1 NAME John /Smith/
1 SEX M
1 BIRT
2 DATE 15 JAN 1950
2 PLAC Boston, Massachusetts, USA
1 OCCU Software Engineer
1 FAMC @F1@
1 FAMS @F2@

0 @F1@ FAM
1 HUSB @I1@
1 WIFE @I2@
1 CHIL @I3@
1 MARR
2 DATE 10 JUN 1975

0 TRLR
```

**Key Record Types:**
- `INDI` - Individual (person) records
- `FAM` - Family (relationship grouping) records
- `HEAD` - Header with metadata
- `TRLR` - Trailer (end marker)

**Data Mapping (Vamsa to GEDCOM):**
| Vamsa Field | GEDCOM Tag |
|-------------|------------|
| firstName + lastName | NAME |
| gender | SEX |
| dateOfBirth | BIRT/DATE |
| birthPlace | BIRT/PLAC |
| dateOfPassing | DEAT/DATE |
| profession | OCCU |
| bio | NOTE |
| Relationship (SPOUSE) | FAM record |
| Relationship (PARENT/CHILD) | FAMC/FAMS links |

---

### Architecture

#### Backend Components

1. **GEDCOM Parser** (`/src/lib/gedcom/parser.ts`)
   - Parse GEDCOM text format into structured objects
   - Handle character encoding (UTF-8, ANSEL)
   - Support GEDCOM 5.5.1 tags
   - Error handling for malformed files

2. **Data Mapper** (`/src/lib/gedcom/mapper.ts`)
   - Map GEDCOM INDI records to vamsa Person model
   - Map GEDCOM FAM records to vamsa Relationship model
   - Handle date format conversion (GEDCOM dates to ISO dates)
   - Handle missing/partial data gracefully

3. **GEDCOM Generator** (`/src/lib/gedcom/generator.ts`)
   - Convert vamsa data to GEDCOM format
   - Generate proper ID references (@I1@, @F1@)
   - Build FAM records from spouse/parent-child relationships
   - Include proper header and trailer

4. **Server Actions** (`/src/actions/gedcom.ts`)
   - `validateGedcom(formData)` - Validate uploaded .ged file
   - `importGedcom(formData, options)` - Import GEDCOM data
   - `exportGedcom()` - Export all data as GEDCOM

5. **API Routes**
   - `/api/admin/gedcom/export` - Download GEDCOM file
   - `/api/admin/gedcom/validate` - Validate GEDCOM upload

#### Frontend Components

1. **GEDCOM Export Component** (`/src/components/admin/gedcom-export.tsx`)
   - Export button with download functionality
   - Progress indicator

2. **GEDCOM Import Component** (`/src/components/admin/gedcom-import.tsx`)
   - File upload form (.ged files)
   - Validation preview
   - Import options (merge strategy)
   - Import progress and results

3. **GEDCOM Page** (`/src/app/(dashboard)/admin/gedcom/page.tsx`)
   - Combined import/export interface
   - Similar layout to backup page

#### Schemas

1. **GEDCOM Schema** (`/src/schemas/gedcom.ts`)
   - Zod schemas for parsed GEDCOM structures
   - Validation result types
   - Import/export option types

---

### Sub-Beads to Create

#### 1. Backend Bead: GEDCOM Parser and Data Processing

**ID:** vamsa-ywo-backend  
**Type:** backend  
**Priority:** P2  
**Parent:** vamsa-ywo

**Scope:**
- Create GEDCOM parser library
- Create data mapper (GEDCOM <-> Vamsa models)

- Create API routes

**Files to Create/Modify:**

- `/src/lib/gedcom/generator.ts` (new)
- `/src/lib/gedcom/types.ts` (new)
- `/src/actions/gedcom.ts` (new)
- `/src/schemas/gedcom.ts` (new)
- `/src/app/api/admin/gedcom/export/route.ts` (new)
- `/src/app/api/admin/gedcom/validate/route.ts` (new)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Parser correctly parses GEDCOM 5.5.1 files with INDI and FAM records
2. Parser handles UTF-8 and common character encodings
3. Parser provides meaningful error messages for malformed files
4. Mapper correctly converts GEDCOM INDI to Person model
5. Mapper correctly infers relationships from FAM records (spouse, parent-child)
6. Mapper handles GEDCOM date formats (DD MMM YYYY, ABT, BEF, AFT)
7. Generator produces valid GEDCOM 5.5.1 output

#### 3. Testing Bead: GEDCOM Tests

**ID:** vamsa-ywo-tests  
**Type:** testing  
**Priority:** P3  
**Parent:** vamsa-ywo

**Scope:**
- Unit tests for GEDCOM parser
- Unit tests for data mapper
- Unit tests for GEDCOM generator
- Integration tests for import/export flow

**Files to Create:**
- `/src/lib/gedcom/parser.test.ts` (new)
- `/src/lib/gedcom/mapper.test.ts` (new)
- `/src/lib/gedcom/generator.test.ts` (new)
- `/src/actions/gedcom.test.ts` (new)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Parser tests cover valid GEDCOM structures
2. Parser tests cover malformed input handling
3. Parser tests cover various date formats
4. Mapper tests verify Person field mapping
5. Mapper tests verify relationship inference
6. Generator tests verify valid GEDCOM output
7. Generator tests verify roundtrip (import then export produces equivalent data)
8. Integration tests use dependency injection pattern (like backup tests)
9. All tests pass with `bun test`

---

### Implementation Notes

1. **Follow existing patterns:**
   - Use dependency injection like `backup.ts` and `restore.ts`
   - Use Zod schemas for validation
   - Use server actions pattern
   - Use TanStack Query for mutations

2. **GEDCOM specifics to handle:**
   - Date approximations (ABT, BEF, AFT, BET...AND)
   - Names with surname delimiters (/Smith/)
   - Cross-references (@I1@, @F1@)
   - Continuation lines (CONC, CONT)
   - Character encoding detection

3. **Edge cases:**
   - People without relationships
   - Multiple marriages
   - Same-sex marriages
   - Unknown genders
   - Partial dates (just year, or month/year)

---

### Summary

| Bead ID | Type | Description | Files |
|---------|------|-------------|-------|
| vamsa-ywo-backend | backend | GEDCOM parser, mapper, generator, actions, API | 8 new files |
| vamsa-ywo-frontend | frontend | Admin page, export/import components | 4 new, 1 modified |
| vamsa-ywo-tests | testing | Unit and integration tests | 4 new files |

---

## Refined GEDCOM Import/Export Implementation Plan

Based on the GEDCOM Wikipedia documentation, I have updated the implementation plan for `vamsa-ywo`. Here is the refined plan:

### Version Strategy

**Primary Target: GEDCOM 5.5.1 Final (November 2019)**
- This is the industry de facto standard used by Ancestry, FamilySearch, Gramps, and most genealogy software
- GEDCOM 7.0 support can be added later but is not blocking for MVP

---

### Data Model Mapping

The key insight from the wiki is that GEDCOM uses a **nuclear family model** with FAM records linking individuals:

| Vamsa Field | GEDCOM Tag | Notes |
|-------------|------------|-------|
| Person | INDI | Individual record |
| firstName + lastName | NAME | Format: `Given /Surname/` |
| gender (MALE) | SEX M | |
| gender (FEMALE) | SEX F | |
| gender (OTHER/PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY) | SEX X | Non-binary or omit |
| dateOfBirth | BIRT > DATE | Birth event |
| birthPlace | BIRT > PLAC | Birth place |
| dateOfPassing | DEAT > DATE | Death event |
| profession | OCCU | Occupation |
| bio | NOTE | With CONC/CONT for multiline |
| Relationship (SPOUSE) | FAM with HUSB/WIFE | |
| Relationship (PARENT/CHILD) | FAM with CHIL + FAMC/FAMS | |

**Important**: HUSB/WIFE are positional tags, not gendered roles. Same-sex couples are fully supported.

---

### Character Encoding Handling

Per GEDCOM 5.5.1 specification:

1. **Detection**: Read HEAD > CHAR tag to determine encoding
2. **Supported encodings**: 
   - UTF-8 (preferred)
   - ANSEL (legacy - needs conversion)
   - ASCII (subset of UTF-8)
3. **Export**: Always use UTF-8

The parser will:
1. Parse header first to detect encoding
2. If ANSEL detected, re-decode entire file
3. Convert all text to UTF-8 internally

---

### GEDCOM Tags Supported

**Level 0 (Top-level)**
- `HEAD` - Header with metadata
- `INDI` - Individual records
- `FAM` - Family group records  
- `TRLR` - End of file marker

**Individual Tags**
- `NAME` - Full name with /surname/ delimiters
- `SEX` - Gender (M/F/X)
- `BIRT` - Birth event with DATE and PLAC
- `DEAT` - Death event with DATE and PLAC
- `OCCU` - Occupation
- `NOTE` - Notes/biography
- `FAMC` - Link to family as child
- `FAMS` - Link to family as spouse
- `CONC/CONT` - Continuation lines

**Family Tags**
- `HUSB` - Partner 1 reference
- `WIFE` - Partner 2 reference
- `CHIL` - Child reference
- `MARR` - Marriage event with DATE
- `DIV` - Divorce event

---

### Date Format Handling

GEDCOM dates are flexible. The parser will handle:

**Exact dates**:
- `1 JAN 2000` - Full date
- `JAN 2000` - Month and year
- `2000` - Year only

**Approximate dates**:
- `ABT 1950` - About/approximately
- `BEF 1950` - Before
- `AFT 1950` - After
- `BET 1950 AND 1960` - Range

**Import Strategy**: Parse all formats, extract best available date components
**Export Strategy**: Use `D MMM YYYY` for full dates, `YYYY` for year-only

---

### Explicitly Out of Scope (MVP)

Per the wiki guidance, these are excluded:

1. **OBJE** - Multimedia objects (can make files enormous)
2. **SOUR** - Source citations (too complex for MVP)
3. **GEDZip** - Multimedia archive format
4. **GEDCOM 7.0** - Future version features
5. **REPO** - Repository records
6. **SUBM** - Submitter records (will use placeholder)

---

### Edge Cases to Handle

1. **Same-sex partnerships** - HUSB/WIFE indicate position only
2. **Unknown genders** - Map to SEX X
3. **Partial dates** - Year-only or month/year
4. **Date approximations** - ABT, BEF, AFT, BET...AND
5. **People without relationships** - Export as standalone INDI
6. **Multiple marriages** - Multiple FAMS links per person
7. **Divorced couples** - isActive=false maps to DIV event

---

### Roundtrip Validation Testing

Per wiki emphasis, this is critical:

**Test**: Import -> Export -> Re-import should preserve:
- All person names and genders
- Birth/death dates and places
- Family relationships (spouse, parent-child)
- Occupations and notes

**Target**: 0% data loss for supported fields

**Test fixtures needed**:
- Minimal valid GEDCOM (1 person)
- Complex multi-generation family
- Same-sex couples and unknown genders
- Various encodings (UTF-8, ANSEL, ASCII)
- All date formats
- Large file (100+ individuals)

---

**Core Library** (`src/lib/gedcom/`):
- `types.ts` - GEDCOM data types
- `parser.ts` - GEDCOM parser (import)
- `generator.ts` - GEDCOM generator (export)
- `encoding.ts` - Encoding detection/conversion
- `date-parser.ts` - GEDCOM date parsing
- `date-formatter.ts` - GEDCOM date formatting
- `mapper.ts` - GEDCOM <-> Vamsa conversion

**Server Actions & API**:
- `src/actions/gedcom.ts` - Server actions
- `src/schemas/gedcom.ts` - Validation schemas
- `src/app/api/admin/gedcom/import/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/admin/gedcom/export/route.ts`

**Frontend Components**:
- `src/components/gedcom/import-dialog.tsx`
- `src/components/gedcom/export-button.tsx`

**Tests** (`src/lib/gedcom/`):
- `parser.test.ts`
- `generator.test.ts`
- `encoding.test.ts`
- `date-parser.test.ts`
- `date-formatter.test.ts`
- `roundtrip.test.ts`
- `test-fixtures/` - Sample GEDCOM files

---

### Implementation Phases

| Phase | Focus | Agent |
|-------|-------|-------|
| 1 | Core Parser (types, line parser, record builder, encoding) | Backend |
| 2 | Date Handling (parser + formatter) | Backend |
| 3 | Data Mapping (bidirectional GEDCOM <-> Vamsa) | Backend |
| 4 | Generator (GEDCOM file output) | Backend |
| 5 | Server Actions & API routes | Backend |
| 6 | UI Components (import dialog, export button) | Frontend |
| 7 | Integration & Roundtrip Testing | Tester |

---

Description:
# GEDCOM Import/Export - Refined Implementation Plan

## Overview
Implement GEDCOM 5.5.1 standard support for family tree data exchange, enabling interoperability with other genealogy software (Ancestry, FamilySearch, Gramps, etc.).

## Version Strategy
- **Primary Target**: GEDCOM 5.5.1 Final (Nov 2019) - industry de facto standard
- **Future**: GEDCOM 7.0 support can be added later (not blocking)

---

## Data Model Mapping

### Vamsa -> GEDCOM
| Vamsa               | GEDCOM Tag    | Notes                                    |
|---------------------|---------------|------------------------------------------|
| Person              | INDI          | Individual record                        |
| firstName + lastName| NAME          | Full name with /surname/ delimiters      |
| gender (MALE)       | SEX M         |                                          |
| gender (FEMALE)     | SEX F         |                                          |
| gender (OTHER)      | SEX X         | Non-binary/unknown                       |
| dateOfBirth         | BIRT > DATE   | Birth event with date                    |
| birthPlace          | BIRT > PLAC   | Birth event with place                   |
| dateOfPassing       | DEAT > DATE   | Death event with date                    |
| profession          | OCCU          | Occupation                               |
| bio                 | NOTE          | Notes/biography                          |
| isLiving            | (implied)     | DEAT present = deceased                  |

### GEDCOM Nuclear Family Model -> Vamsa
GEDCOM uses FAM (family) records to link individuals:
- FAM record with HUSB/WIFE pointers = SPOUSE relationship in Vamsa
- CHIL pointer in FAM = child belongs to that family
- FAMC in INDI = "family as child" - links person to parents
- FAMS in INDI = "family as spouse" - links person to partner(s)

**Important**: HUSB/WIFE are positional, NOT gendered. Modern parsers should not infer gender from these tags.

---

## Supported GEDCOM Tags

### Level 0 (Top-level records)
- `HEAD` - Header with metadata (charset, version, source)
- `INDI` - Individual person record
- `FAM` - Family group record
- `TRLR` - Trailer (end of file marker)

### Individual (INDI) Tags
- `NAME` - Full name (format: "Given /Surname/")
- `SEX` - Gender (M/F/X)
- `BIRT` - Birth event
- `DEAT` - Death event
- `OCCU` - Occupation
- `NOTE` - Notes/bio (with CONC/CONT for multiline)
- `FAMC` - Family where person is child
- `FAMS` - Family where person is spouse

### Event Sub-tags
- `DATE` - Date of event
- `PLAC` - Place of event

### Family (FAM) Tags
- `HUSB` - Reference to partner 1
- `WIFE` - Reference to partner 2
- `CHIL` - Reference to child
- `MARR` - Marriage event (with DATE)
- `DIV` - Divorce event (with DATE)

### Continuation Tags
- `CONC` - Continuation (no line break)
- `CONT` - Continuation with line break

---

## Date Format Support

GEDCOM dates are flexible. Must handle:

### Exact Dates
- `1 JAN 2000` - Day Month Year
- `JAN 2000` - Month Year only
- `2000` - Year only

### Approximate Dates
- `ABT 1950` - About/approximately
- `BEF 1950` - Before
- `AFT 1950` - After
- `BET 1950 AND 1960` - Between range

### Implementation
- Import: Parse all formats, store best available date
- Export: Use exact format `D MMM YYYY` when full date available, `YYYY` for year-only

---

## Character Encoding

### GEDCOM 5.5.1 Requirements
- Support both ANSEL (legacy) and UTF-8 encodings
- Detect encoding from HEAD > CHAR tag
- Convert ANSEL to UTF-8 on import

### Detection Strategy
1. Read HEAD record first
2. Check CHAR tag value: "UTF-8", "ANSEL", "ASCII"
3. Default to UTF-8 if unspecified
4. Re-decode file content if ANSEL detected

### Export
- Always export as UTF-8 (modern standard)
- Set `1 CHAR UTF-8` in header

---

## Out of Scope (MVP)

- **OBJE** - Multimedia objects (photos, documents)
- **SOUR** - Source citations and references
- **GEDZip** - Multimedia archive format
- **GEDCOM 7.0** - Future version (can add later)
- **REPO** - Repository records
- **SUBM** - Submitter records (will use placeholder)

---

## Edge Cases to Handle

1. **Same-sex partnerships**: HUSB/WIFE indicate position, not gender
2. **Unknown genders**: Map to SEX X
3. **Partial dates**: Year-only, month/year
4. **People without relationships**: Export as standalone INDI
5. **Multiple marriages**: Multiple FAMS links per person
6. **Divorced couples**: isActive=false maps to DIV event
7. **PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY gender**: Map to SEX X (or omit SEX tag)

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Import
1. Parse valid GEDCOM 5.5.1 files
2. Detect and handle UTF-8 and ANSEL encodings
3. Create Person records for each INDI
4. Create Relationship records from FAM links
5. Handle all date formats (partial, approximate)
6. Handle CONC/CONT continuation lines
7. Validate file structure (HEAD, TRLR present)
8. Return meaningful errors for invalid files
9. Support files up to 10MB

### Export
1. Generate valid GEDCOM 5.5.1 output
2. Export all Person records as INDI
3. Generate FAM records for spouse relationships
4. Include children in appropriate FAM records
5. Use UTF-8 encoding
6. Include proper header with source info

### Roundtrip Validation
1. Import -> Export -> Import should preserve:
   - All person names and genders
   - Birth/death dates and places
   - Family relationships (spouse, parent-child)
   - Occupations and notes
2. Maximum acceptable data loss: 0% for supported fields
3. Test with sample files from major genealogy software

---

## Files to Create/Modify

### New Files
- `src/lib/gedcom/types.ts` - GEDCOM data types
- `src/lib/gedcom/parser.ts` - GEDCOM parser (import)
- `src/lib/gedcom/generator.ts` - GEDCOM generator (export)
- `src/lib/gedcom/encoding.ts` - Encoding detection/conversion
- `src/lib/gedcom/date-parser.ts` - GEDCOM date parsing
- `src/lib/gedcom/date-formatter.ts` - GEDCOM date formatting
- `src/lib/gedcom/mapper.ts` - GEDCOM <-> Vamsa conversion
- `src/actions/gedcom.ts` - Server actions
- `src/schemas/gedcom.ts` - Validation schemas
- `src/app/api/admin/gedcom/import/route.ts` - Import endpoint
- `src/app/api/admin/gedcom/export/route.ts` - Export endpoint
- `src/components/gedcom/import-dialog.tsx` - Import UI
- `src/components/gedcom/export-button.tsx` - Export UI

### Test Files
- `src/lib/gedcom/parser.test.ts` - Parser tests
- `src/lib/gedcom/generator.test.ts` - Generator tests
- `src/lib/gedcom/encoding.test.ts` - Encoding tests
- `src/lib/gedcom/date-parser.test.ts` - Date parsing tests
- `src/lib/gedcom/date-formatter.test.ts` - Date formatting tests
- `src/lib/gedcom/roundtrip.test.ts` - Roundtrip validation
- `src/lib/gedcom/test-fixtures/` - Sample GEDCOM files

### Modify
- `src/app/(dashboard)/settings/page.tsx` - Add import/export UI

---

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Tests
- Parser: Line parsing, record building, tag handling
- Date parser: All date formats and approximations
- Encoding: UTF-8 detection, ANSEL conversion
- Generator: Valid GEDCOM output structure
- Mapper: Bidirectional data conversion

### Integration Tests
- Full import flow (file -> database)
- Full export flow (database -> file)
- Roundtrip preservation tests

### Test Fixtures
- Minimal valid GEDCOM (1 person)
- Complex family (multiple generations)
- Edge cases (same-sex couples, unknown genders)
- Various encodings (UTF-8, ANSEL, ASCII)
- Different date formats
- Large file (100+ individuals)
- Files from Ancestry, FamilySearch, Gramps (if available)

---

## Implementation Order

1. **Phase 1: Core Parser** (Backend)
   - Types and data structures
   - Line-level parser
   - Record builder
   - Encoding detection

2. **Phase 2: Date Handling** (Backend)
   - Date parser (all formats)
   - Date formatter (export)

3. **Phase 3: Data Mapping** (Backend)
   - GEDCOM -> Vamsa mapper
   - Vamsa -> GEDCOM mapper

4. **Phase 4: Generator** (Backend)
   - GEDCOM file generator
   - Header/trailer generation

5. **Phase 5: Server Actions & API** (Backend)
   - Import action with validation
   - Export action
   - API routes

6. **Phase 6: UI Components** (Frontend)
   - Import dialog with file picker
   - Export button
   - Progress/error feedback

7. **Phase 7: Integration** (Testing)
   - Roundtrip tests
   - Edge case validation
   - Performance testing

Children (5):
  ↳ vamsa-ywo.10: GEDCOM Import/Export UI [P2 - closed]
  ↳ vamsa-ywo.6: GEDCOM Parser and Data Types [P2 - closed]
  ↳ vamsa-ywo.7: GEDCOM Data Mapper (GEDCOM ↔ Vamsa) [P2 - closed]
  ↳ vamsa-ywo.8: GEDCOM Generator and Server Actions [P2 - closed]
  ↳ vamsa-ywo.9: GEDCOM Roundtrip Tests [P2 - closed]

# GEDCOM Test Fixtures

Comprehensive test data for GEDCOM 5.5.1 import/export functionality.

## Overview

This directory contains 10 real-world GEDCOM fixture files that cover various scenarios for meaningful testing of the import/export feature.

## Fixtures

### 1. simple-person.ged
**Size**: 259 bytes | **Entities**: 1 person

A single person with all common fields:
- Name: John Smith
- Gender: Male
- Birth: 15 JAN 1950 in Boston, Massachusetts, USA
- Profession: Software Engineer
- Notes: Single biographical note

**Use case**: Testing basic import/export with single individual

### 2. three-generation.ged
**Size**: 805 bytes | **Entities**: 6 people + 2 families

Three-generation family structure:
- **Generation 1**: John Smith (m) + Mary Johnson (f) - married 1945
- **Generation 2**: Robert Smith - their child
- **Generation 3**: David Smith + Elizabeth Smith - Robert's children

Demonstrates:
- Multi-generational parent-child relationships
- Spouse relationships with marriage dates
- Death dates
- FAMC/FAMS references

**Use case**: Testing complex family structures and relationship mapping

### 3. multiple-marriages.ged
**Size**: 888 bytes | **Entities**: 7 people + 2 families

Person with two marriages:
- **William Anderson** marries Dorothy Brown (1963, divorced 1973)
  - Children: James, Patricia
- **William Anderson** marries Margaret Davis (1980)
  - Children: Charles, Helen

Demonstrates:
- Multiple FAMS references in single person
- Divorce dates
- Children from different marriages
- No relationship confusion between families

**Use case**: Testing multiple marriage scenarios and FAMS handling

### 4. same-sex-couple.ged
**Size**: 420 bytes | **Entities**: 3 people + 1 family

Same-gender couple with child:
- **Michael Johnson** (m) + **Christopher Lee** (m) - married 2001
- Child: Emma Johnson (f)

Demonstrates:
- Two males as HUSB/WIFE (positional, not gendered)
- Same-sex couple not misinterpreted as parent-child
- Proper family structure

**Use case**: Testing gender handling and modern family structures

### 5. date-formats.ged
**Size**: 552 bytes | **Entities**: 7 people

Tests various GEDCOM date formats:
- Full date: 15 JAN 1985
- Month/year: JAN 1985
- Year only: 1985
- Approximate: ABT 1985
- Before: BEF 1980
- After: AFT 1990
- Between: BET 1975 AND 1985

**Use case**: Testing date parsing for all GEDCOM formats

### 6. special-names.ged
**Size**: 468 bytes | **Entities**: 5 people

Names with special characters:
- José García (accents)
- Marie-Claire Dubois (hyphen)
- Patrick O'Brien (apostrophe)
- Müller Von Bergen (umlaut + spaces)
- Jean-Pierre De La Cruz (complex multi-part)

Demonstrates:
- UTF-8 encoding handling
- International character support
- Name parsing with special characters
- Complex surname patterns

**Use case**: Testing UTF-8 encoding and international names

### 7. long-notes.ged
**Size**: 551 bytes | **Entities**: 1 person

Extended biography with CONT continuation lines:
- Alexander Hamilton
- Multi-line note spanning 5 continuation lines
- Historical biographical information

Demonstrates:
- CONT tag handling
- Line continuation and concatenation
- Multi-line note preservation

**Use case**: Testing continuation line handling and long text

### 8. sparse-data.ged
**Size**: 234 bytes | **Entities**: 3 people

Minimal data with missing optional fields:
- Person 1: Name only
- Person 2: Name + gender
- Person 3: Name + birth year only

Demonstrates:
- Graceful handling of missing fields
- No required fields except name
- Sparse data parsing

**Use case**: Testing robustness with incomplete data

### 9. large-family.ged
**Size**: 3.6 KB | **Entities**: 22+ people + 5 families

Comprehensive multi-generational family:
- 2 grandparents
- 4 children with different spouses
- 10+ grandchildren
- Multiple professions and places
- Complex relationship network

Demonstrates:
- Scaling with 20+ individuals
- Multiple family units
- Complex relationship networks
- Full biographical details

**Use case**: Testing performance and complex relationships at scale

### 10. full-details.ged
**Size**: 619 bytes | **Entities**: 2 people + 1 family

Complete biographical information:
- **Benjamin Franklin**
  - Birth: 17 JAN 1706 in Boston, Massachusetts, USA
  - Death: 17 APR 1790 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA
  - Professions: Printer, Publisher, Scientist, Diplomat
  - Notes: Founding Father and polymath
- **Deborah Read**
  - Birth: 1707 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA
  - Death: 1774 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA
- Married: 1730 in Philadelphia

Demonstrates:
- Complete biographical data
- Multiple professions
- Birth and death places
- Marriage with location
- Historical context in notes

**Use case**: Testing full data preservation

## Usage

### Import fixtures in tests

```typescript
import { fixtures } from './fixtures'

describe('GEDCOM Parser', () => {
  test('parses simple person', () => {
    const content = fixtures.simplePerson()
    const parser = new GedcomParser()
    const result = parser.parse(content)
    expect(result.individuals).toHaveLength(1)
  })
})
```

### Roundtrip testing

```typescript
test('three-generation family survives roundtrip', () => {
  const original = fixtures.threeGeneration()

  // Parse
  const parsed = parser.parse(original)

  // Map to Vamsa
  const mapped = mapper.mapFromGedcom(parsed)

  // Map back to GEDCOM
  const remapped = mapper.mapToGedcom(mapped.people, mapped.relationships)

  // Generate
  const generated = generator.generate(remapped.individuals, remapped.families)

  // Re-parse
  const reparsed = parser.parse(generated)

  // Verify data preserved
  expect(reparsed.individuals).toHaveLength(parsed.individuals.length)
  expect(reparsed.families).toHaveLength(parsed.families.length)
})
```

| sparse-data | ✓ | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | ✓ | - |
| large-family | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | - | ✓ | ✓ | - | - | - | ✓ |
| full-details | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | - | - | ✓ | - | ✓ | - | - |

## Testing Scenarios

### Parser Testing
- Use `simple-person` for basic parsing
- Use `date-formats` for date parsing variations
- Use `special-names` for UTF-8 and character handling
- Use `long-notes` for continuation line handling
- Use `sparse-data` for edge case handling

### Mapper Testing
- Use `three-generation` for relationship mapping
- Use `multiple-marriages` for FAMS handling
- Use `same-sex-couple` for gender handling
- Use `full-details` for all data mapping

### Generator Testing
- Use `simple-person` for basic output
- Use `large-family` for scaling
- Use `special-names` for UTF-8 output
- Use `long-notes` for CONT tag generation

### Roundtrip Testing
- Use all fixtures for complete roundtrip verification
- Verify no data loss through import→export→reimport
- Verify semantic equivalence through export→import→export

### UI Testing
- Use `simple-person` for basic import dialog
- Use `multiple-marriages` for complex preview
- Use `sparse-data` for error handling
- Use `large-family` for performance testing

## File Locations

All fixtures are in:
```
src/lib/gedcom/__tests__/fixtures/
├── index.ts
├── simple-person.ged
├── three-generation.ged
├── multiple-marriages.ged
├── same-sex-couple.ged
├── date-formats.ged
├── special-names.ged
├── long-notes.ged
├── sparse-data.ged
├── large-family.ged
└── full-details.ged
```

## Standards Compliance

All fixtures follow **GEDCOM 5.5.1 Final** (November 2019) specification:
- Proper line structure with level, tag, optional xref, optional value
- Valid xref format: `@I\d+@`, `@F\d+@`
- UTF-8 encoding declared in header
- All required records: HEAD, TRLR
- Valid tag nesting and hierarchy
- Proper date formatting

## Adding New Fixtures

To add a new fixture:
1. Create `new-scenario.ged` with valid GEDCOM 5.5.1 content
2. Add export to `index.ts`: `newScenario: () => fs.readFileSync(...)`
3. Document in this file with size, entities, and use cases
4. Add to coverage matrix

## References

- GEDCOM 5.5.1 Specification: https://edge.fscdn.org/assets/img/documents/ged551-5bac5e57fe88dd37df0e153d9c515335.pdf
- FamilySearch GEDCOM GitHub: https://github.com/FamilySearch/GEDCOM/tree/main/specification

- Dates preserved

### 5. Export & Re-import

3. Import `exported.ged` back

    })

## Troubleshooting

- Check file is valid GEDCOM 5.5.1
- Verify HEAD and TRLR present
- Check for malformed xrefs
- Use `parser.validate()` for detailed errors

### Names not displaying correctly

Based on the GEDCOM Wikipedia documentation provided, refine the implementation plan for vamsa-ywo (GEDCOM Import/Export).

Key insights from the wiki to incorporate:

1. **Version Strategy**: Support GEDCOM 5.5.1 final (released Nov 2019) as the primary target since it's the industry de facto standard. This is what most genealogy software uses. Optional: Consider GEDCOM 7.0 future support but don't block on it.

2. **Character Encoding**: 
   - GEDCOM 5.5.1 supports both ANSEL (legacy) and UTF-8
   - GEDCOM 7.0 requires UTF-8 only

## GEDCOM Import/Export - Updated MVP Plan

Based on your feedback, I have revised the implementation plan to focus on a simpler, more focused MVP with roundtrip testing as the primary success criteria.

---

### Scope Summary

| In Scope (MVP) | Explicitly Deferred (Phase 2) |
|----------------|------------------------------|
| GEDCOM 5.5.1 only | GEDCOM 7.0 support |
| UTF-8 encoding only | ANSEL encoding detection/conversion |
| INDI (Individual) records | Multimedia objects (OBJE) |
| FAM (Family) records | Source citations (SOUR) |
| Essential tags (NAME, SEX, BIRT, DEAT, OCCU, NOTE, FAMC, FAMS, HUSB, WIFE, CHIL, MARR, DIV) | Continuation line optimizations |
| Date parsing (D MMM YYYY, ABT, BEF, AFT, BET...AND) | Advanced validation features |
| Roundtrip test suite | |
| Simple error handling | |

---

### Reference Specification

**GitHub**: https://github.com/FamilySearch/GEDCOM/tree/main/specification

This will be the authoritative source for implementation details during development.

---

### Implementation Architecture

Following the existing backup/restore patterns in the codebase:

```
src/lib/gedcom/
  types.ts           # TypeScript types for GEDCOM structures
  parser.ts          # GEDCOM 5.5.1 text -> internal structure
  mapper.ts          # Internal structure <-> Vamsa data model
  generator.ts       # Vamsa data -> GEDCOM 5.5.1 text
  date-parser.ts     # GEDCOM date format handling

src/schemas/
  gedcom.ts          # Zod validation schemas

src/actions/
  gedcom.ts          # Server actions (import/export)

src/app/api/admin/gedcom/
  export/route.ts    # GET - download .ged file
  import/route.ts    # POST - upload and process

src/components/admin/
  gedcom-export.tsx  # Export UI
  gedcom-import.tsx  # Import UI with preview
```

---

### Data Mapping (GEDCOM <-> Vamsa)

| GEDCOM | Vamsa Person | Notes |
|--------|--------------|-------|
| `NAME /Surname/Given` | firstName, lastName | Parse name parts |
| `SEX M/F` | gender | Map to MALE/FEMALE |
| `BIRT.DATE` | dateOfBirth | Parse GEDCOM date format |
| `DEAT.DATE` | dateOfPassing, isLiving=false | |
| `BIRT.PLAC` | birthPlace | |
| `OCCU` | profession | |
| `NOTE` | bio | Concatenate multiple notes |

| GEDCOM | Vamsa Relationship | Notes |
|--------|-------------------|-------|
| `FAM.HUSB/WIFE` | type=SPOUSE | Create bidirectional |
| `FAM.CHIL` | type=PARENT/CHILD | Parent refs child, child refs parent |
| `FAM.MARR.DATE` | marriageDate | On SPOUSE relationship |
| `FAM.DIV.DATE` | divorceDate, isActive=false | |

---

### Roundtrip Testing Strategy (Primary Success Criteria)

**Test Loop 1: Import -> Export -> Re-import**
```
1. Import sample.ged into Vamsa
2. Export Vamsa data to exported.ged
3. Re-import exported.ged into fresh database
4. Compare: original import data == re-import data
```

**Test Loop 2: Export -> Import -> Export**
```
1. Create test data in Vamsa
2. Export to export1.ged
3. Clear database, import export1.ged
4. Export again to export2.ged
5. Compare: export1.ged == export2.ged (normalized)
```

**Test Data**:
- Family with 3 generations (grandparents, parents, children)
- Multiple marriages (with divorce)
- Various date formats (exact, ABT, BEF, AFT, BET...AND)
- Names with maiden names
- Notes and occupations

# GEDCOM Import/Export - Refined Implementation Plan

## Overview
Implement GEDCOM 5.5.1 standard support for family tree data exchange, enabling interoperability with other genealogy software (Ancestry, FamilySearch, Gramps, etc.).

## Version Strategy
- **Primary Target**: GEDCOM 5.5.1 Final (Nov 2019) - industry de facto standard
- **Future**: GEDCOM 7.0 support can be added later (not blocking)

---

## Data Model Mapping

### Vamsa -> GEDCOM
| Vamsa               | GEDCOM Tag    | Notes                                    |
|---------------------|---------------|------------------------------------------|
| Person              | INDI          | Individual record                        |
| firstName + lastName| NAME          | Full name with /surname/ delimiters      |
| gender (MALE)       | SEX M         |                                          |
| gender (FEMALE)     | SEX F         |                                          |
| gender (OTHER)      | SEX X         | Non-binary/unknown                       |
| dateOfBirth         | BIRT > DATE   | Birth event with date                    |
| birthPlace          | BIRT > PLAC   | Birth event with place                   |
| dateOfPassing       | DEAT > DATE   | Death event with date                    |
| profession          | OCCU          | Occupation                               |
| bio                 | NOTE          | Notes/biography                          |
| isLiving            | (implied)     | DEAT present = deceased                  |

### GEDCOM Nuclear Family Model -> Vamsa
GEDCOM uses FAM (family) records to link individuals:
- FAM record with HUSB/WIFE pointers = SPOUSE relationship in Vamsa
- CHIL pointer in FAM = child belongs to that family
- FAMC in INDI = "family as child" - links person to parents
- FAMS in INDI = "family as spouse" - links person to partner(s)

**Important**: HUSB/WIFE are positional, NOT gendered. Modern parsers should not infer gender from these tags.

---

## Supported GEDCOM Tags

### Level 0 (Top-level records)
- `HEAD` - Header with metadata (charset, version, source)
- `INDI` - Individual person record
- `FAM` - Family group record
- `TRLR` - Trailer (end of file marker)

### Individual (INDI) Tags
- `NAME` - Full name (format: "Given /Surname/")
- `SEX` - Gender (M/F/X)
- `BIRT` - Birth event
- `DEAT` - Death event
- `OCCU` - Occupation
- `NOTE` - Notes/bio (with CONC/CONT for multiline)
- `FAMC` - Family where person is child
- `FAMS` - Family where person is spouse

### Event Sub-tags
- `DATE` - Date of event
- `PLAC` - Place of event

### Family (FAM) Tags
- `HUSB` - Reference to partner 1
- `WIFE` - Reference to partner 2
- `CHIL` - Reference to child
- `MARR` - Marriage event (with DATE)
- `DIV` - Divorce event (with DATE)

### Continuation Tags
- `CONC` - Continuation (no line break)
- `CONT` - Continuation with line break

---

## Date Format Support

GEDCOM dates are flexible. Must handle:

### Exact Dates
- `1 JAN 2000` - Day Month Year
- `JAN 2000` - Month Year only
- `2000` - Year only

### Approximate Dates
- `ABT 1950` - About/approximately
- `BEF 1950` - Before
- `AFT 1950` - After
- `BET 1950 AND 1960` - Between range

### Implementation
- Import: Parse all formats, store best available date
- Export: Use exact format `D MMM YYYY` when full date available, `YYYY` for year-only

---

## Character Encoding

### GEDCOM 5.5.1 Requirements
- Support both ANSEL (legacy) and UTF-8 encodings
- Detect encoding from HEAD > CHAR tag
- Convert ANSEL to UTF-8 on import

### Detection Strategy
1. Read HEAD record first
2. Check CHAR tag value: "UTF-8", "ANSEL", "ASCII"
3. Default to UTF-8 if unspecified
4. Re-decode file content if ANSEL detected

### Export
- Always export as UTF-8 (modern standard)
- Set `1 CHAR UTF-8` in header

---

## Out of Scope (MVP)

- **OBJE** - Multimedia objects (photos, documents)
- **SOUR** - Source citations and references
- **GEDZip** - Multimedia archive format
- **GEDCOM 7.0** - Future version (can add later)
- **REPO** - Repository records
- **SUBM** - Submitter records (will use placeholder)

---

## Edge Cases to Handle

1. **Same-sex partnerships**: HUSB/WIFE indicate position, not gender
2. **Unknown genders**: Map to SEX X
3. **Partial dates**: Year-only, month/year
4. **People without relationships**: Export as standalone INDI
5. **Multiple marriages**: Multiple FAMS links per person
6. **Divorced couples**: isActive=false maps to DIV event
7. **PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY gender**: Map to SEX X (or omit SEX tag)

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Import
1. Parse valid GEDCOM 5.5.1 files
2. Detect and handle UTF-8 and ANSEL encodings
3. Create Person records for each INDI
4. Create Relationship records from FAM links
5. Handle all date formats (partial, approximate)
6. Handle CONC/CONT continuation lines
7. Validate file structure (HEAD, TRLR present)
8. Return meaningful errors for invalid files
9. Support files up to 10MB

### Export
1. Generate valid GEDCOM 5.5.1 output
2. Export all Person records as INDI
3. Generate FAM records for spouse relationships
4. Include children in appropriate FAM records
5. Use UTF-8 encoding
6. Include proper header with source info

### Roundtrip Validation
1. Import -> Export -> Import should preserve:
   - All person names and genders
   - Birth/death dates and places
   - Family relationships (spouse, parent-child)
   - Occupations and notes
2. Maximum acceptable data loss: 0% for supported fields
3. Test with sample files from major genealogy software

---

## Files to Create/Modify

### New Files
- `src/lib/gedcom/types.ts` - GEDCOM data types
- `src/lib/gedcom/parser.ts` - GEDCOM parser (import)
- `src/lib/gedcom/generator.ts` - GEDCOM generator (export)
- `src/lib/gedcom/encoding.ts` - Encoding detection/conversion
- `src/lib/gedcom/date-parser.ts` - GEDCOM date parsing
- `src/lib/gedcom/date-formatter.ts` - GEDCOM date formatting
- `src/lib/gedcom/mapper.ts` - GEDCOM <-> Vamsa conversion
- `src/actions/gedcom.ts` - Server actions
- `src/schemas/gedcom.ts` - Validation schemas
- `src/app/api/admin/gedcom/import/route.ts` - Import endpoint
- `src/app/api/admin/gedcom/export/route.ts` - Export endpoint
- `src/components/gedcom/import-dialog.tsx` - Import UI
- `src/components/gedcom/export-button.tsx` - Export UI

### Test Files
- `src/lib/gedcom/parser.test.ts` - Parser tests
- `src/lib/gedcom/generator.test.ts` - Generator tests
- `src/lib/gedcom/encoding.test.ts` - Encoding tests
- `src/lib/gedcom/date-parser.test.ts` - Date parsing tests
- `src/lib/gedcom/date-formatter.test.ts` - Date formatting tests
- `src/lib/gedcom/roundtrip.test.ts` - Roundtrip validation
- `src/lib/gedcom/test-fixtures/` - Sample GEDCOM files

### Modify
- `src/app/(dashboard)/settings/page.tsx` - Add import/export UI

---

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Tests
- Parser: Line parsing, record building, tag handling
- Date parser: All date formats and approximations
- Encoding: UTF-8 detection, ANSEL conversion
- Generator: Valid GEDCOM output structure
- Mapper: Bidirectional data conversion

### Integration Tests
- Full import flow (file -> database)
- Full export flow (database -> file)

- Files from Ancestry, FamilySearch, Gramps (if available)

---

## Implementation Order

1. **Phase 1: Core Parser** (Backend)
   - Types and data structures
   - Line-level parser
   - Record builder
   - Encoding detection

2. **Phase 2: Date Handling** (Backend)
   - Date parser (all formats)

   - GEDCOM -> Vamsa mapper
   - Vamsa -> GEDCOM mapper

4. **Phase 4: Generator** (Backend)
   - GEDCOM file generator
   - Header/trailer generation

5. **Phase 5: Server Actions & API** (Backend)
   - Import action with validation
   - Export action
   - API routes

6. **Phase 6: UI Components** (Frontend)
   - Import dialog with file picker
   - Export button
   - Progress/error feedback

7. **Phase 7: Integration** (Testing)
   - Roundtrip tests

# GEDCOM Test Fixtures

Comprehensive test data for GEDCOM 5.5.1 import/export functionality.

## Overview

This directory contains 10 real-world GEDCOM fixture files that cover various scenarios for meaningful testing of the import/export feature.

## Fixtures

### 1. simple-person.ged
**Size**: 259 bytes | **Entities**: 1 person

A single person with all common fields:
- Name: John Smith
- Gender: Male
- Birth: 15 JAN 1950 in Boston, Massachusetts, USA
- Profession: Software Engineer
- Notes: Single biographical note

**Use case**: Testing basic import/export with single individual

### 2. three-generation.ged
**Size**: 805 bytes | **Entities**: 6 people + 2 families

Three-generation family structure:
- **Generation 1**: John Smith (m) + Mary Johnson (f) - married 1945
- **Generation 2**: Robert Smith - their child
- **Generation 3**: David Smith + Elizabeth Smith - Robert's children

Demonstrates:
- Multi-generational parent-child relationships
- Spouse relationships with marriage dates
- Death dates
- FAMC/FAMS references

**Use case**: Testing complex family structures and relationship mapping

### 3. multiple-marriages.ged
**Size**: 888 bytes | **Entities**: 7 people + 2 families

Person with two marriages:
- **William Anderson** marries Dorothy Brown (1963, divorced 1973)
  - Children: James, Patricia
- **William Anderson** marries Margaret Davis (1980)
  - Children: Charles, Helen

Demonstrates:
- Multiple FAMS references in single person
- Divorce dates
- Children from different marriages
- No relationship confusion between families

**Use case**: Testing multiple marriage scenarios and FAMS handling

### 4. same-sex-couple.ged
**Size**: 420 bytes | **Entities**: 3 people + 1 family

Same-gender couple with child:
- **Michael Johnson** (m) + **Christopher Lee** (m) - married 2001
- Child: Emma Johnson (f)

Demonstrates:
- Two males as HUSB/WIFE (positional, not gendered)
- Same-sex couple not misinterpreted as parent-child
- Proper family structure

**Use case**: Testing gender handling and modern family structures

### 5. date-formats.ged
**Size**: 552 bytes | **Entities**: 7 people

Tests various GEDCOM date formats:
- Full date: 15 JAN 1985
- Month/year: JAN 1985
- Year only: 1985
- Approximate: ABT 1985
- Before: BEF 1980
- After: AFT 1990
- Between: BET 1975 AND 1985

**Use case**: Testing date parsing for all GEDCOM formats

### 6. special-names.ged
**Size**: 468 bytes | **Entities**: 5 people

Names with special characters:
- José García (accents)
- Marie-Claire Dubois (hyphen)
- Patrick O'Brien (apostrophe)
- Müller Von Bergen (umlaut + spaces)
- Jean-Pierre De La Cruz (complex multi-part)

Demonstrates:
- UTF-8 encoding handling
- International character support
- Name parsing with special characters
- Complex surname patterns

**Use case**: Testing UTF-8 encoding and international names

### 7. long-notes.ged
**Size**: 551 bytes | **Entities**: 1 person

Extended biography with CONT continuation lines:
- Alexander Hamilton
- Multi-line note spanning 5 continuation lines
- Historical biographical information

Demonstrates:
- CONT tag handling
- Line continuation and concatenation
- Multi-line note preservation

**Use case**: Testing continuation line handling and long text

### 8. sparse-data.ged
**Size**: 234 bytes | **Entities**: 3 people

Minimal data with missing optional fields:
- Person 1: Name only
- Person 2: Name + gender
- Person 3: Name + birth year only

Demonstrates:
- Graceful handling of missing fields
- No required fields except name
- Sparse data parsing

**Use case**: Testing robustness with incomplete data

### 9. large-family.ged
**Size**: 3.6 KB | **Entities**: 22+ people + 5 families

Comprehensive multi-generational family:
- 2 grandparents
- 4 children with different spouses
- 10+ grandchildren
- Multiple professions and places
- Complex relationship network

Demonstrates:
- Scaling with 20+ individuals
- Multiple family units
- Complex relationship networks
- Full biographical details

**Use case**: Testing performance and complex relationships at scale

### 10. full-details.ged
**Size**: 619 bytes | **Entities**: 2 people + 1 family

Complete biographical information:
- **Benjamin Franklin**
  - Birth: 17 JAN 1706 in Boston, Massachusetts, USA
  - Death: 17 APR 1790 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA
  - Professions: Printer, Publisher, Scientist, Diplomat
  - Notes: Founding Father and polymath
- **Deborah Read**
  - Birth: 1707 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA
  - Death: 1774 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA
- Married: 1730 in Philadelphia

Demonstrates:
- Complete biographical data
- Multiple professions
- Birth and death places
- Marriage with location
- Historical context in notes

**Use case**: Testing full data preservation

## Usage

### Import fixtures in tests

```typescript
import { fixtures } from './fixtures'

describe('GEDCOM Parser', () => {
  test('parses simple person', () => {
    const content = fixtures.simplePerson()
    const parser = new GedcomParser()
    const result = parser.parse(content)
    expect(result.individuals).toHaveLength(1)
  })
})
```

### Roundtrip testing

```typescript
test('three-generation family survives roundtrip', () => {
  const original = fixtures.threeGeneration()

  // Parse
  const parsed = parser.parse(original)

  // Map to Vamsa
  const mapped = mapper.mapFromGedcom(parsed)

  // Map back to GEDCOM
  const remapped = mapper.mapToGedcom(mapped.people, mapped.relationships)

  // Generate
  const generated = generator.generate(remapped.individuals, remapped.families)

  // Re-parse
  const reparsed = parser.parse(generated)

  // Verify data preserved
  expect(reparsed.individuals).toHaveLength(parsed.individuals.length)
  expect(reparsed.families).toHaveLength(parsed.families.length)
})
```

## Coverage Matrix

| Fixture | Single Person | Family | Marriage | Divorce | Children | Dates | Special Chars | Notes | Sparse | Large Scale |
|---------|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| simple-person | ✓ | - | - | - | - | ✓ | - | ✓ | - | - |
| three-generation | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | - | ✓ | ✓ | - | - | - | - |
| multiple-marriages | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | - | - | - | - |
| same-sex-couple | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | - | ✓ | ✓ | - | - | - | - |
| date-formats | ✓ | - | - | - | - | ✓ | - | - | - | - |
| special-names | ✓ | - | - | - | - | ✓ | ✓ | - | - | - |
| long-notes | ✓ | - | - | - | - | ✓ | - | ✓ | - | - |
| sparse-data | ✓ | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | ✓ | - |
| large-family | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | - | ✓ | ✓ | - | - | - | ✓ |
| full-details | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | - | - | ✓ | - | ✓ | - | - |

## Testing Scenarios

### Parser Testing
- Use `simple-person` for basic parsing
- Use `date-formats` for date parsing variations
- Use `special-names` for UTF-8 and character handling
- Use `long-notes` for continuation line handling
- Use `sparse-data` for edge case handling

### Mapper Testing
- Use `three-generation` for relationship mapping
- Use `multiple-marriages` for FAMS handling
- Use `same-sex-couple` for gender handling
- Use `full-details` for all data mapping

### Generator Testing
- Use `simple-person` for basic output
- Use `large-family` for scaling
- Use `special-names` for UTF-8 output
- Use `long-notes` for CONT tag generation

### Roundtrip Testing
- Use all fixtures for complete roundtrip verification
- Verify no data loss through import→export→reimport
- Verify semantic equivalence through export→import→export

### UI Testing
- Use `simple-person` for basic import dialog
- Use `multiple-marriages` for complex preview
- Use `sparse-data` for error handling
- Use `large-family` for performance testing

## File Locations

All fixtures are in:
```
src/lib/gedcom/__tests__/fixtures/
├── index.ts
├── simple-person.ged
├── three-generation.ged
├── multiple-marriages.ged
├── same-sex-couple.ged
├── date-formats.ged
├── special-names.ged
├── long-notes.ged
├── sparse-data.ged
├── large-family.ged
└── full-details.ged
```

## Standards Compliance

All fixtures follow **GEDCOM 5.5.1 Final** (November 2019) specification:
- Proper line structure with level, tag, optional xref, optional value
- Valid xref format: `@I\d+@`, `@F\d+@`
- UTF-8 encoding declared in header
- All required records: HEAD, TRLR
- Valid tag nesting and hierarchy
- Proper date formatting

## Adding New Fixtures

To add a new fixture:
1. Create `new-scenario.ged` with valid GEDCOM 5.5.1 content
2. Add export to `index.ts`: `newScenario: () => fs.readFileSync(...)`
3. Document in this file with size, entities, and use cases
4. Add to coverage matrix

## References

- GEDCOM 5.5.1 Specification: https://edge.fscdn.org/assets/img/documents/ged551-5bac5e57fe88dd37df0e153d9c515335.pdf
- FamilySearch GEDCOM GitHub: https://github.com/FamilySearch/GEDCOM/tree/main/specification

# GEDCOM Phase 2 - Enhancement Roadmap

Phase 2 enhancements for the GEDCOM import/export feature, focusing on character encoding support, GEDCOM 7.0 compatibility, and advanced features.

## Overview

Phase 1 delivered a complete GEDCOM 5.5.1 MVP with UTF-8 support. Phase 2 expands capabilities while maintaining backward compatibility with Phase 1.

## Phase 2 Features

### 1. ANSEL Encoding Support (Priority: HIGH)

**Context:**
- GEDCOM 5.5.1 supports both UTF-8 and ANSEL (legacy LDS encoding)
- Many genealogy software still exports ANSEL (especially older versions)
- ANSEL files are common in genealogy community
- Phase 1 assumes UTF-8 only

**Implementation:**
Create `src/lib/gedcom/encoding.ts`:
```typescript
export class GedcomEncoding {
  /**
   * Detect encoding from HEAD > CHAR tag
   */
  detectEncoding(content: string): 'UTF-8' | 'ANSEL' | 'ASCII' {
    // Read first 500 bytes to find HEAD record
    // Parse CHAR tag value
    // Return detected encoding (default UTF-8)
  }

  /**
   * Convert ANSEL to UTF-8
   * ANSEL is a 8-bit character set with custom mappings
   */
  anselToUtf8(anselText: string): string {
    // Map ANSEL character codes to Unicode
    // Handle multi-byte sequences
    // Return UTF-8 string
  }

  /**
   * Convert UTF-8 to ANSEL (for export compatibility)
   */
  utf8ToAnsel(utf8Text: string): string {
    // Map Unicode to ANSEL where possible
    // Fallback to placeholder for unmappable chars
    // Return ANSEL string
  }
}
```

**Files to Create/Modify:**
- `src/lib/gedcom/encoding.ts` (new) - ANSEL/UTF-8 conversion
- `src/lib/gedcom/encoding.test.ts` (new) - Encoding tests
- `src/lib/gedcom/parser.ts` (modify) - Add encoding detection
- `src/lib/gedcom/__tests__/fixtures/ansel-encoded.ged` (new) - ANSEL test fixture

**Test Data:**
Create fixture with ANSEL encoding:
- Names with accents (Müller, José, François)
- Non-ASCII characters (®, ©, etc.)
- Verify roundtrip: ANSEL → UTF-8 → export

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Detect CHAR tag values: UTF-8, ANSEL, ASCII
- [ ] Convert ANSEL to UTF-8 on import
- [ ] Handle all ANSEL character mappings
- [ ] Preserve special characters through conversion
- [ ] Export to ANSEL for compatibility (optional)
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Backward compatible with Phase 1

---

### 2. GEDCOM 7.0 Support (Priority: MEDIUM)

**Context:**
- GEDCOM 7.0 released May 2021
- Addresses shortcomings in 5.5.1
- Improved multimedia support, better date handling
- New event types (explicit event non-existence)
- Better extensibility with standard way to mark extensions
- FamilySearch committed to 7.0 by Q3 2022 (not yet achieved)

**Key Differences from 5.5.1:**
- UTF-8 mandatory (no ANSEL)
- New DATE format: ISO 8601 (2021-05-27 instead of 27 MAY 2021)
- GEDCOM 7.0 version in header
- Better multimedia handling (OBJE can have FILE and linked format)
- More event types
- Can explicitly mark events as non-existent (e.g., FACT about never marrying)
- Extensions must have standard prefix

**Implementation:**
Create version-agnostic parser:
```typescript
export type GedcomVersion = '5.5.1' | '7.0'

export interface GedcomParserOptions {
  version?: GedcomVersion
  strict?: boolean // Strict vs lenient parsing
}

export class GedcomParser {
  parse(content: string, options?: GedcomParserOptions): GedcomFile {
    // Auto-detect version from HEAD > GEDC > VERS
    // Parse according to detected/specified version
    // Handle version differences gracefully
  }
}
```

**Files to Create/Modify:**
- `src/lib/gedcom/types.ts` (modify) - Add version info
- `src/lib/gedcom/parser.ts` (modify) - Add version detection/handling
- `src/lib/gedcom/generator.ts` (modify) - Generate 7.0 format option
- `src/lib/gedcom/date-parser.ts` (modify) - Add ISO 8601 date support
- `src/lib/gedcom/parser.test.ts` (modify) - Add 7.0 tests
- `src/lib/gedcom/__tests__/fixtures/gedcom70-sample.ged` (new)

**Features to Add:**
- [ ] Detect GEDCOM version from header
- [ ] Parse GEDCOM 7.0 date format (ISO 8601)
- [ ] Generate ISO 8601 dates on export to 7.0
- [ ] Handle new GEDCOM 7.0 event types
- [ ] Support GEDCOM 7.0 FILE structure for multimedia
- [ ] Validate GEDCOM 7.0 syntax rules
- [ ] Option to export as GEDCOM 7.0

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Parse both 5.5.1 and 7.0 files correctly
- [ ] Auto-detect version from header
- [ ] ISO 8601 date parsing and generation
- [ ] Handle 7.0-specific features gracefully
- [ ] Backward compatible with Phase 1 (default 5.5.1)
- [ ] Export option for 7.0 format
- [ ] All tests pass

---

### 3. Source Citations Support (Priority: MEDIUM)

**Context:**
- SOUR (Source) records document where info came from
- Critical for genealogical research credibility
- Wiki notes: Can cause data duplication and maintenance issues
- Out of scope for MVP, but valuable for Phase 2

**Implementation:**
Create source citation support:
```typescript
export interface ParsedSource {
  id: string
  title: string
  author?: string
  publicationInfo?: string
  repository?: string
  notes: string[]
}

export interface CitationReference {
  sourceId: string
  page?: string
  eventType?: string // BIRT, DEAT, etc.
  notes?: string
}
```

**Files to Create:**
- `src/lib/gedcom/source-parser.ts` - Parse SOUR records
- `src/lib/gedcom/source-mapper.ts` - Map to Vamsa
- `src/lib/gedcom/source.test.ts` - Tests
- Database schema update for sources

**Vamsa Integration:**
Add to `Person` model:
```prisma
model Person {
  // ... existing fields
  eventSources  EventSource[]
}

model EventSource {
  id        String
  personId  String
  person    Person      @relation(fields: [personId], references: [id])
  eventType String      // BIRT, DEAT, etc
  sourceId  String
  pageInfo  String?
  createdAt DateTime    @default(now())
}
```

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Parse SOUR records from GEDCOM
- [ ] Link citations to events (BIRT, DEAT, etc.)
- [ ] Store source information in database
- [ ] Export sources back to GEDCOM
- [ ] Handle multiple citations per event
- [ ] All tests pass

---

### 4. Multimedia Object Support (Priority: LOW)

**Context:**
- OBJE (Object) records reference photos, documents, etc.
- Phase 1 excluded multimedia (can make files enormous)
- Phase 2 can add support for linked references

**Scope (Minimal):**
Support external file references only (not embedded):
```
0 @O1@ OBJE
1 FILE /path/to/photo.jpg
1 FORM JPEG
1 TITLE Portrait of John Smith
```

**Implementation:**
Add minimal OBJE support:
```typescript
export interface ParsedObject {
  id: string
  filePath: string
  format: string // JPEG, GIF, PNG, etc.
  title?: string
  notes: string[]
}
```

**Scope Out:**
- Embedded objects (base64 encoded in file)
- GEDZip (zip archive with media)
- Actual file storage/management

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Parse OBJE references
- [ ] Store metadata (file path, format, title)
- [ ] Link to individuals/events
- [ ] Export OBJE references (don't create files)
- [ ] All tests pass

---

### 5. Additional Event Types (Priority: LOW)

**Context:**
- GEDCOM 5.5.1 has limited event types
- GEDCOM 7.0 expands significantly
- Can add common events for better data capture

**Events to Add:**
- Engagement (ENGM)
- Divorce filing (DIVF)
- Adoption (ADOP)
- Confirmation (CONF)
- Graduation (GRAD)
- Immigration (IMMI)
- Emigration (EMIG)
- Naturalization (NATU)
- Residence (RESI)
- Custom events (_CUSTOM)

**Implementation:**
Create event type mapper:
```typescript
export const GEDCOM_EVENTS = {
  BIRT: 'Birth',
  DEAT: 'Death',
  MARR: 'Marriage',
  DIV: 'Divorce',
  ENGM: 'Engagement',
  DIVF: 'Divorce Filing',
  ADOP: 'Adoption',
  CONF: 'Confirmation',
  GRAD: 'Graduation',
  IMMI: 'Immigration',
  EMIG: 'Emigration',
  NATU: 'Naturalization',
  RESI: 'Residence',
}
```

---

### 6. Repository & Submitter Records (Priority: LOW)

**Context:**
- REPO (Repository) records reference where source came from
- SUBM (Submitter) records identify who submitted data
- Phase 1 used placeholder
- Can improve source tracking in Phase 2

**Implementation:**
Parse and store:
- Repository information
- Submitter contact info
- Data modification history

---

## Implementation Priority

### High Priority (Complete by next release)
1. **ANSEL Encoding** - Many existing GEDCOM files use it
2. **GEDCOM 7.0 Detection** - At least auto-detect and warn

### Medium Priority (Next quarter)
3. **GEDCOM 7.0 Full Support** - Full read/write compatibility
4. **Source Citations** - Important for genealogy research

### Low Priority (Nice to have)
5. **Multimedia Support** - External references only
6. **Additional Events** - Expand beyond BIRT/DEAT/MARR
7. **Repository/Submitter** - Better metadata tracking

## Deferred (Beyond Phase 2)
- Embedded multimedia (OBJE with embedded files)
- GEDZip format support
- Advanced validation rules
- GEDCOM X format
- Multi-language support

## Testing Strategy for Phase 2

### New Test Fixtures
```
src/lib/gedcom/__tests__/fixtures/
├── ansel-encoded.ged           # ANSEL encoded fixture
├── gedcom70-sample.ged         # GEDCOM 7.0 format
├── with-sources.ged            # Source citations
├── with-multimedia.ged         # OBJE references
└── mixed-events.ged            # Various event types
```

### Test Coverage Goals
- ANSEL: 100% character mapping coverage
- GEDCOM 7.0: 95%+ parity with 5.5.1
- Sources: Full roundtrip preservation
- Multimedia: Reference preservation

## Backward Compatibility

All Phase 2 features must:
- ✓ Not break Phase 1 functionality
- ✓ Default to Phase 1 behavior if Phase 2 features not present
- ✓ Work seamlessly with Phase 1 data
- ✓ Support mixed Phase 1/2 files

## Performance Considerations

Phase 2 features should not significantly impact:
- Parse speed: < 100ms for 100+ person files
- Export speed: < 100ms for 100+ person files
- Memory usage: < 50MB for large files

## Documentation

Phase 2 should include:
- [ ] Updated parser documentation
- [ ] ANSEL character mapping reference
- [ ] GEDCOM 7.0 migration guide
- [ ] Source citation best practices
- [ ] Performance benchmarks
- [ ] Troubleshooting guide

## Migration Path

Users with Phase 1 data can:
1. Continue using Phase 1 (always supported)
2. Export as Phase 1 format
3. Opt-in to Phase 2 features (GEDCOM 7.0, sources, etc.)
4. Re-import enhanced files with Phase 2 support

## Estimated Effort

| Feature | Effort | Complexity |
|---------|--------|-----------|
| ANSEL Encoding | 2-3 days | Medium |
| GEDCOM 7.0 Detection | 1 day | Low |
| GEDCOM 7.0 Full Support | 3-4 days | Medium |
| Source Citations | 3-4 days | Medium |
| Multimedia Support | 2-3 days | Low |
| Additional Events | 1-2 days | Low |
| **Total** | **12-18 days** | **Medium** |

## Success Criteria

Phase 2 is complete when:
- [ ] ANSEL files import without errors
- [ ] GEDCOM 7.0 files detected and parsed correctly
- [ ] Sources preserved through roundtrip cycle
- [ ] Multimedia references preserved
- [ ] All tests pass (500+ tests expected)
- [ ] Performance within benchmarks
- [ ] Backward compatible with Phase 1
- [ ] Documentation complete

## Reference Links

- GEDCOM 5.5.1 Spec: https://edge.fscdn.org/assets/img/documents/ged551-5bac5e57fe88dd37df0e153d9c515335.pdf
- GEDCOM 7.0 Spec: https://github.com/FamilySearch/GEDCOM/tree/main/specification
- ANSEL Charset: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSEL
- FamilySearch GEDCOM Docs: https://www.familysearch.org/developers/docs/guides/gedcom

---

## How to Start Phase 2

When ready to begin Phase 2:

1. **Create Epic for Phase 2:**
   ```bash
   bd create --title="GEDCOM Phase 2 - ANSEL & GEDCOM 7.0" \
     --type=epic \
     --priority=2 \
     --description="Phase 2 enhancements: ANSEL encoding, GEDCOM 7.0, sources, multimedia"
   ```

2. **Create Sub-beads:**
   ```bash
   bd create --title="ANSEL Encoding Support" --type=task --priority=0 --parent=<phase2-epic>
   bd create --title="GEDCOM 7.0 Support" --type=task --priority=1 --parent=<phase2-epic>
   bd create --title="Source Citations" --type=task --priority=1 --parent=<phase2-epic>
   bd create --title="Multimedia Support" --type=task --priority=2 --parent=<phase2-epic>
   ```

3. **Start with ANSEL:**
   ```bash
   @backend implement ANSEL encoding support
   ```

Good luck with Phase 2! 🚀
